body:
## Problem

Every `Ctrl+V` paste in a terminal pane sends the clipboard content twice to the PTY.

## Root Cause

`attachCustomKeyEventHandler` returning `false` tells xterm.js not to process the keydown event, but it does **not** call `e.preventDefault()` on the underlying DOM event. The browser therefore continues with its native paste action and fires:

```
beforeinput(insertFromPaste) → paste
```

The existing `beforeinput` handler on xterm's hidden textarea intercepts this and sends the pasted text through the WebSocket a second time — resulting in every `Ctrl+V` delivering the text twice.

## Fix

Call `e.preventDefault()` in the `Ctrl+V` branch of the custom key handler. This cancels the browser's native paste action before it starts, so only `pasteFromClipboard()` sends the text. `Cmd+V` on macOS is covered by the same branch via `e.metaKey`.

```js
if (mod && e.key === 'v') {
  e.preventDefault();   // ← added
  this.pasteFromClipboard();
  return false;
}
```

## Testing

- `Ctrl+V` with text in clipboard → pastes once
- `Cmd+V` on macOS → pastes once
- Right-click → Paste → still works (unaffected path)
- Bracketed paste mode preserved (pasteFromClipboard wraps in `\x1b[200~...\x1b[201~`)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: fix: prevent Ctrl+V double-paste in terminal panes

## Summary This PR tightens up the Projects left sidebar with five focused design improvements, then adds optional Lucide icon support so workspaces can show a meaningful icon in place of the color dot. --- ## Screenshots ### Project list with icons assigned --- ### Icon picker in the Edit Project modal --- ## Changes ### 1. Session count as inline badge The "3 sessions" subtitle text under each workspace name is replaced by a compact pill badge rendered inline next to the name. This reduces vertical height of each workspace row and removes a line of low-signal text. **Before:** Two-line layout — name on top, "3 sessions" beneath. **After:** Single-line — `project-name ●3` with the badge sitting mid-line. ### 2. Active left-bar indicator uses workspace color The 3px left-edge highlight on the active workspace previously used the global `--accent` color for every workspace. It now reads `--ws-color` (a CSS custom property set inline on the workspace item element), so each workspace's active state reflects its own color. This required no JavaScript change — the color is passed as `style="--ws-color: ${color}"` on the item element, and the `::before` pseudo-element picks it up via `background: var(--ws-color, var(--accent))`. ### 3. Directory sub-group headers: lighter and simpler The directory group headers (e.g. `▶ repos/sidecar-dev 3`) previously had a boxy hover background and used the full monospace + subtext styling. They now: - Have no hover background (just a color shift from `--overlay0` to `--subtext0`) - Are italic to visually separate them from session items - Lose the pill background on the session count — just a plain number - Slightly reduced padding (4px → 2px vertical) ### 4. Session items: sans-serif name, time inline Session rows previously used monospace for the name and placed last-active time in a separate meta row. Now: - Name uses the default sans-serif (more readable at small sizes) - Last-active time sits right-aligned inline with the name (`margin-left: auto`) - The meta row (badges, size) only renders when there is actually something to show, eliminating empty whitespace for sessions with no badges ### 5. Single `…` more button The two icon buttons (✏️ rename, 🗑️ delete) that appeared on hover are replaced by a single `…` button. Clicking it opens the existing context menu system (`_renderContextItems`) anchored to the button, with **Rename** and **Delete** as items. This reduces visual clutter on hover and is consistent with how other menus work in the app. --- ## Lucide icon support ### Dependencies ``` lucide ^1.8.0 (MIT) @lucide/lab ^0.1.2 (ISC) ``` ### How the bundle works `scripts/build-lucide-bundle.mjs` is a Node.js build script (no additional build tooling required — it reads the raw ESM icon source files directly). It: 1. Reads `node_modules/lucide/dist/esm/icons/.js` for each icon in the curated list 2. Evaluates the icon data array (using Node's `vm.runInNewContext` — the format is JS object literals, not JSON) 3. Serializes each icon to an inline SVG string with `stroke="currentColor"` so color is controlled via CSS 4. Writes `src/web/public/vendor/lucide.bundle.js` — a plain IIFE that sets `window.__lucideIcons` and `window.__lucideIconCategories`, then dispatches `lucide-ready` To regenerate after a lucide version upgrade: ```bash npm run build:icons ``` The bundle is ~62KB and covers **140 icons** in 11 categories: | Category | Count | Example icons | |---|---|---| | Folders & Files | 14 | `folder`, `folder-code`, `folder-git-2`, `file-code` | | Code & Dev | 12 | `code`, `terminal`, `git-branch`, `braces` | | Infrastructure | 12 | `database`, `server`, `cloud`, `network` | | Apps & Tools | 13 | `package`, `workflow`, `settings`, `hammer` | | Design & Art | 12 | `palette`, `wand-sparkles`, `pen-tool`, `camera` | | Learning & Science | 12 | `brain`, `flask-conical`, `microscope`, `atom` | | People & Status | 15 | `user`, `bot`, `rocket`, `shield`, `trophy` | | Home & Work | 11 | `house`, `briefcase`, `landmark`, `compass` | | Media & Comms | 12 | `monitor`, `mail`, `music`, `headphones` | | Nature & Fun | 17 | `flame`, `coffee`, `leaf`, `cat`, `rabbit` | | Lab Extras | 10 | `owl`, `planet`, `bee`, `venn` (from `@lucide/lab`) | ### Data model `icon` is an optional string field on the workspace object (stored in `~/.myrlin/workspaces.json`). It holds the kebab-case icon name (e.g. `"folder-code"`) or `null`. Existing workspaces without an `icon` field continue to show the color dot unchanged. ### Icon picker UI The modal icon field renders a live-filterable grid grouped by category. Typing in the search box filters icons by name and hides category headers with no visible results. The "No icon" option (a dashed circle) is always first and resets the workspace to the plain color dot. ### Rendering In `renderWorkspaceItem()`: ```js ws.icon && window.__lucideIcons?.[ws.icon] ? `${window.__lucideIcons[ws.icon]}` : `
` ``` The icon SVG uses `stroke="currentColor"`, so the workspace color flows through via `style="color: ${color}"` on the wrapper — no additional CSS variables needed. --- ## Test plan - [ ] Existing workspaces (no `icon` set) still show the color dot — no regression - [ ] Create new workspace → icon picker appears in modal; selecting "No icon" creates workspace with color dot - [ ] Create workspace with icon → icon appears in sidebar colored with the chosen workspace color - [ ] Edit workspace → current icon is pre-selected in the picker; changing it saves correctly; clearing to "No icon" removes the icon - [ ] Icon search: typing filters icons; clearing search restores all; category headers hide/show correctly - [ ] Active left-bar color matches workspace color in all cases (with icon and without) - [ ] `…` more button: click opens context menu with Rename/Delete; both actions work - [ ] Session items: time is inline; meta row absent when no badges; name is sans-serif - [ ] Directory group headers: lighter/italic; no boxy hover background - [ ] `npm run build:icons` regenerates the bundle cleanly
title: feat: sidebar design polish + Lucide icon picker for workspaces

body: ## Summary This PR adds a full **Tasks view** to the workspace manager — a dedicated tab (alongside Projects, Terminal, etc.) that gives you a heads-up display of everything happening in a project: worktree tasks, td issues, git status/diffs, and a live file editor. Several bugs discovered during development are also fixed. --- ## What's new ### Tasks view tab strip A new top-level nav tab (**Tasks**) hosts four sub-tabs: | Tab | What it shows | |-----|--------------| | **Worktree Tasks** | Board/list view of Claude worktree tasks with kanban columns (Backlog → Planning → Running → Review → Done) and a searchable list view | | **td** | td issues grouped by status (In Progress → In Review → Blocked → Open), sorted by priority within each group, with a modal for full issue context including logs | | **Git** | Branch indicator, staged/modified/untracked file list with inline diffs, recent commit log — clicking a commit row shows the full `git show` diff in the right pane | | **Files** | Two-pane file explorer + CodeMirror 6 editor with syntax highlighting and atomic save | Switching projects in the sidebar immediately refreshes whichever sub-tab is active. --- ### Git tab — commit diff viewer Clicking a commit row in the log now shows the full `git show` output (stat + patch) in the right pane. The hash badge still copies to clipboard on click (`stopPropagation` prevents double-triggering). The 10-second auto-refresh preserves the right pane via `cloneNode` so the diff isn't wiped while you're reading it; the selected row is re-highlighted after each refresh. **New endpoint:** `GET /api/git/commit-diff?workspaceId=&hash=` --- ### Files tab — CodeMirror served locally CodeMirror 6 is now bundled with esbuild and served from `vendor/codemirror.bundle.js` instead of being fetched from `esm.sh` at runtime. This fixes failures for users whose browser doesn't have direct internet access (e.g. accessing the app via Tailscale or a private network). No CDN dependency at runtime. --- ### td tab — friendly "not initialized" state When td isn't initialized for a project, instead of a cryptic error string the td tab now shows: - A plain-language explanation - A hint about git worktrees (if the session is in a worktree, td should be initialized in the main repo) - A **Run `td init`** button that calls `POST /api/workspaces/:id/td/init` and refreshes the panel on success --- ### td tab — issue detail modal with logs `td show --json` returns `description: ""` with all content in the `logs[]` array. The issue detail modal now renders a **Log** section with timestamps and type tags (decision, blocker, etc.) so you can read full task history inline. --- ### Tasks tab layout fix `session-list-panel` now starts with `hidden` in the HTML. Previously it was visible before JS ran, causing the Projects panel to flash at the top of the page the first time the Tasks tab was opened. --- ## Bug fixes | # | Bug | Fix | |---|-----|-----| | 1 | `GET /api/git/status` and `/api/git/branches` returned 400 "dir query parameter required" when called with `workspaceId` | Added `workspaceId` → `resolveWorkspaceDir()` fallback in both routes | | 2 | Duplicate `/api/git/status` and `/api/git/branches` routes shadowed the fixed ones | Removed unreachable duplicate routes | | 3 | `/api/git/log` and `/api/git/diff` used `ws.workingDir` (undefined on workspace objects) | Switched to `resolveWorkspaceDir()` | | 4 | CodeMirror failed to load via `import()` from a classic script context | Replaced with `

## Summary

The mobile app has excellent cross-platform code (all Expo libraries are Android-compatible, biometrics/push/SSE/QR scanning all work on both platforms), but the Android configuration in `app.json` and `eas.json` was incomplete enough that an EAS Android build would fail and several runtime features would silently break.

### Changes

**`mobile/app.json`**
- Added `package: "io.myrlin.workbook"` (mirrors iOS `bundleIdentifier` — required for EAS to generate the APK/AAB)
- Added `versionCode: 1` (required by Google Play)
- Added `targetSdkVersion: 35` / `minSdkVersion: 24` (Android 7.0+, covers ~99% of active devices)
- Added `permissions` array for all features the app uses:
  - `CAMERA` — QR code pairing
  - `RECORD_AUDIO` — voice commands in terminal
  - `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` / `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` — image uploads to sessions
  - `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` — push notifications (required on API 33+)
  - `INTERNET` / `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` / `CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE` — server connectivity

**`mobile/eas.json`**
- Added `buildType: "aab"` to the `production` profile (Google Play Store requires AAB, not APK)

**`mobile/maestro/config.yaml`**
- Fixed `appId` from `com.myrlin.mobile` → `io.myrlin.workbook` to match the package name; all 18 Maestro flows were referencing the wrong ID and would fail to launch the app on Android

## What's still needed before Play Store submission

These require external resources I can't add here:
- **Firebase/FCM setup**: `push-service.ts` has the Android notification channel wired up correctly, but FCM credentials need to be added to EAS for push notifications to actually deliver on Android
- **Notification status bar icon**: A small monochrome PNG at `assets/images/notification-icon.png` + `android.notification.icon` in `app.json` — without it Android uses the app icon (which may look blurry in the status bar)

## Test plan

- [ ] `eas build --platform android --profile development` should now produce an APK without errors
- [ ] Install APK on Android device and verify permission prompts appear for camera, microphone, and notifications
- [ ] Maestro flows should now launch correctly on Android (`maestro test mobile/maestro/flows/`)
- [ ] `eas build --platform android --profile production` should produce an AAB

body:
## Summary
- Block xterm.js native paste handling (`beforeinput` with `insertFromPaste`) since we handle Ctrl+V/Cmd+V manually via `pasteFromClipboard()`
- Without this fix, pasted text was sent twice via WebSocket, causing duplicate input in the terminal

## Root cause
When pasting text:
1. Our `attachCustomKeyEventHandler` intercepts Ctrl+V and calls `pasteFromClipboard()` → sends text via WebSocket
2. xterm.js also receives the native `beforeinput` event with `insertFromPaste` and fires `onData` → sends text again

## Fix
Block `insertFromPaste` events in the `beforeinput` listener with `{ capture: true }` to intercept before xterm.js processes them.
title: fix: prevent double paste in terminal input

## Summary

- Replaces outdated hardcoded model version IDs with the official Claude Code model aliases across all model picker locations
- Adds all 6 aliases from the [Claude Code model config docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config#model-aliases)
- Fixes shell glob expansion bug where `sonnet[1m]` was being mangled by bash before reaching `claude`

| Alias | Description |
|---|---|
| `default` | Recommended model for your account type |
| `opus` | Latest Opus — complex reasoning |
| `sonnet` | Latest Sonnet — daily coding |
| `haiku` | Fast and efficient — simple tasks |
| `sonnet[1m]` | Sonnet with 1M token context window |
| `opusplan` | Opus for plan mode, Sonnet for execution |

## Bug fixed

`pty-manager.js` was building the command as:
```
bash -l -c "claude --model sonnet[1m]"
```
Bash interprets `[1m]` as a glob character class, silently mangling the alias before it reaches `claude`. Fixed by single-quoting the model value.

## Locations updated

- Launcher modal `<select>` (`index.html`)
- Session context menu model submenu (`app.js`)
- Task context menu model submenu (`app.js`)
- Template / new task form model select (`app.js`)
- Settings → Default Model (Planning) and Default Model (Running) (`app.js`)
- PTY command builder — model value now shell-quoted (`pty-manager.js`)

## Why aliases over full IDs

Aliases always resolve to the latest model version automatically. Hardcoded IDs go stale when Anthropic releases new models.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open launcher → Model dropdown shows all 6 options
- [ ] Launch with `Sonnet 1M` → session starts, `claude --model 'sonnet[1m]'` is passed correctly
- [ ] Launch with `OpusPlan` → session starts on opusplan mode
- [ ] Right-click a session → Model submenu shows all 6 options
- [ ] Settings → Advanced → Default Model dropdowns show updated options

body:
## Summary

Addresses review feedback — replaces plaintext password in the startup URL with a one-time, time-limited token.

- **One-time startup token**: `generateStartupToken()` creates a random token stored in a `startupTokens` Map with 60s TTL and single-use enforcement. The startup URL now uses `?token=<random>` instead of `?password=<actual-password>`.
- **New endpoint**: `POST /api/auth/token-login` exchanges a startup token for a session Bearer token. Rate-limited, validates expiry and single-use. Token is deleted from the map immediately after use.
- **`AUTH_PASSWORD` no longer exported** — stays module-private in auth.js, reducing attack surface.
- **Memory cleanup**: background interval (every 5 min) removes expired/used startup tokens, matching the existing `loginAttempts` cleanup pattern.
- **Extracted `_initializeApp()`** in app.js to eliminate 3x copy-paste of the post-login init sequence (was duplicated in `init()`, `login()`, and `tokenLogin()`).
- **Stale token handling**: token login is always attempted when a URL token is present, even if a cached session token exists in localStorage (handles server restart gracefully).

### Security improvements over v1
| Concern | Before (v1) | After (v2) |
|---------|-------------|------------|
| Console logs | Plaintext password in URL | One-time token (safe to leak) |
| `AUTH_PASSWORD` scope | Exported, accessible from other modules | Module-private |
| Timing window | Password in `window.location.search` until `replaceState` | Token is single-use — even if captured, can't be reused |
| Replay attack | Same URL works forever | Token expires after 60s and is deleted after first use |

## Files changed
- `src/web/auth.js` — token generation, cleanup interval, `POST /api/auth/token-login`, removed `AUTH_PASSWORD` export
- `src/gui.js` — uses `generateStartupToken()` instead of `AUTH_PASSWORD`
- `src/web/public/app.js` — handles `?token=`, new `tokenLogin()` method, extracted `_initializeApp()`
- `test/run.js` — updated 6 URL extraction tests (password→token), added 4 server-side token tests
- `README.md` — updated documentation

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` passes (52/52 tests)
- [x] Start server: `CWM_PASSWORD=test123 PORT=40932 node src/gui.js`
- [x] Console prints URL with `?token=<random>` (not `?password=`)
- [x] Click URL — auto-login works via token-login endpoint
- [x] Reuse same token — rejected ("Invalid or expired startup token")
- [x] Invalid token — rejected
- [x] Normal form login with password still works
- [x] `AUTH_PASSWORD` is `undefined` in auth.js exports
title: Replace password-in-URL with one-time startup token

![A nicely wrapped gift is opened — and shoots flour in the recipient's face](https://media.giphy.com/media/u36K6jl0KkYcJAdvhN/giphy.gif)

*A gift — with flour. The integration works great, but it surfaced several bugs in the worktree task flow that are also submitted as standalone PRs (#21–#25) if you want to review them independently.*

---

## What this adds

Optional integration with [td](https://github.com/marcus/td), a minimalist CLI task manager built for AI agent workflows. When `td` is installed and initialized in a repo, Myrlin surfaces its issues directly in the docs panel and sidebar — no context-switching to the terminal to check your task list.

**It's entirely opt-in.** The integration is hidden behind a toggle in Settings → "td Task Management". If td isn't installed or the setting is off, nothing in the existing UI changes.

---

## Why td alongside the built-in kanban?

Myrlin's kanban board is excellent for project-level orchestration — creating worktree branches, tracking PR state, running parallel agents. `td` fills a different niche and the two work well together:

| | Myrlin Kanban | td |
|---|---|---|
| **Lives in** | Myrlin's state store | `.todos/` in the repo (committable) |
| **Follows git?** | No | Yes — travels with branches |
| **AI agent access** | Via Myrlin GUI | Via `td` CLI in any terminal |
| **Session isolation** | No | Yes — implementer can't approve own work |
| **Structured handoffs** | No | Yes — `td handoff --done / --remaining / --decision` |
| **Worktree per task** | Yes (Myrlin creates it) | Via Myrlin's "→ Worktree" button |
| **PR tracking** | Yes | No |
| **Cross-context memory** | No | Yes — designed for multi-session AI workflows |

**Use Myrlin's kanban** to orchestrate worktrees, manage dependencies, and coordinate agents at the project level. **Use td** inside those worktrees to track sub-tasks, log decisions, and hand off structured context to the next agent — especially useful when a task spans multiple context windows or needs a separate session to review the work.

The worktree promotion flow ties them together: click "→ Worktree" on any td issue to create a branch + git worktree + Claude session in one click, with the issue description passed as the opening prompt to Claude. Claude starts already briefed on the task.

---

## Files changed

### `src/core/td-adapter.js` *(new file)*
Shell adapter that wraps the `td` binary. Functions: `getStatus()`, `listIssues()`, `getIssue()`, `getContext()`, `initTd()`. All calls use `execFileSync` with the resolved binary path. Returns structured objects or throws with a clear message on failure (binary not found, td not initialized, etc.).

### `src/web/server.js`
Six new API endpoints plus two resolver functions:

- `resolveTdBinaryPath(store, workspaceId)` — tries the user-configured path first, then common install locations (`~/.local/bin/td`, `~/go/bin/td`, `$PATH`). Returns the first working binary path or null.
- `resolveTdRepoDir(store, workspaceId)` — infers which directory holds the `.todos/` folder for a workspace. Checks `workspace.tdRepoDir` first, then falls back to frequency analysis of session `workingDir` values. Uses `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (via `execFileSync`, not a shell template) to correctly resolve worktree session paths to their main repo root — where `.todos/` actually lives.
- `GET /api/workspaces/:id/td/status` — returns `{ available, initialized, version }`. Drives the status badge in the UI.
- `GET /api/workspaces/:id/td/issues` — returns parsed issue list from `td list --json`.
- `GET /api/workspaces/:id/td/issues/:issueId` — single issue detail.
- `GET /api/workspaces/:id/td/issues/:issueId/context` — full `td context` output (done/remaining/decisions/uncertain from previous sessions).
- `POST /api/workspaces/:id/td/init` — runs `td init` in the resolved repo directory.

### `src/state/store.js`
- Adds `enableTd: true` and `tdBinary: ''` to the default settings schema.
- Adds `initialPrompt` and `flags` fields to the session schema so the worktree task creation endpoint can pass the td issue description through to the Claude PTY on first launch.

### `src/web/pty-manager.js`
Two fixes required for the worktree promotion flow:

- Before appending `--continue`, checks `~/.claude/projects/` for a matching JSONL history file. Only adds `--continue` if history actually exists — `claude --continue` exits with code 1 on fresh directories, which was crashing every new worktree task.
- On first client attach (no `resumeSessionId`), reads `initialPrompt` and `flags` from the stored session record and appends them to the command string. Flags become `--flagname` args; the prompt is shell-escaped and appended as a positional argument. Subsequent reconnects skip this so Claude doesn't re-receive the initial task.

### `src/web/public/index.html`
- **td Issues section** inside the docs panel: status badge (installed/not installed, initialized/not initialized), refresh button, and a table of open issues with id, priority, status, and title columns.
- **td issue detail modal**: overlay with a header showing the td badge + issue title + id, a meta row (type, priority, status, assignee), collapsible Details section with the issue description, Context section with the full `td context` output from previous sessions, and a "→ Worktree" promote button in the footer.
- **Sidebar tasks header**: toggle row above the sidebar task list letting you switch between the native tasks view and a td issues view.

## Problem

When promoting a td task to a worktree, if the branch had previously been checked out in a different worktree path, `git worktree add` would fail with:

```
fatal: 'branch' is already checked out at '/some/other/path'
```

The original fix (PR #21) only checked whether the *target path* was already registered. This second error occurs when the *branch* is already registered at a different path.

## Fix

Parse `git worktree list --porcelain` output into blocks and check both conditions in one pass:

1. **Path already registered**: skip `git worktree add`, reuse as-is
2. **Branch checked out at different path**: redirect `worktreePath` to that existing location so session creation and task records point at the right directory

This also subsumes the PR #21 fix (path already exists check) so both cases are handled together.

## Files Changed

- `src/web/server.js` — replace single path-check with full porcelain block parsing

## Problem

`claude --continue` exits with code 1 ("No conversation found to continue") when there is no prior session JSONL file for the working directory. This broke every brand-new worktree task: the terminal would open and connect, then immediately exit with that error.

The comment in the code said Claude would start fresh on an empty directory — but that's not how `--continue` works (or the CLI behavior changed).

## Fix

Before appending `--continue`, scan `~/.claude/projects/` for a directory matching the session's working directory and check whether it contains any `.jsonl` files. Only add `--continue` if history actually exists.

Falls back safely: if the projects directory doesn't exist or the scan fails, `--continue` is omitted and Claude starts fresh.

## Files Changed

- `src/web/pty-manager.js` — check for JSONL history before adding `--continue`

## Problem

`store.createSession` takes a single destructured object argument:

```js
createSession({ name, workspaceId, workingDir, command, ... })
```

Two call sites in `server.js` were incorrectly passing `workspaceId` as a separate first argument:

```js
// Wrong — workspaceId ends up undefined inside the function
store.createSession(workspaceId, { name, workingDir, command })
```

This caused `this._state.workspaces[undefined]` to always return falsy, so `createSession` returned `null` and the endpoint responded with `"Failed to create session"` every time.

Affected endpoints:
- `POST /api/worktree-tasks` (worktree task creation)
- Spinoff task creation flow

## Fix

Move `workspaceId` inside the options object at both call sites, matching the function signature and the correct usage already present elsewhere in the codebase.

## Testing

- Create a worktree task via the UI — session should be created successfully
- Spinoff task creation should also work correctly

title: fix: pass workspaceId inside object to store.createSession

Thanks for developing and sharing this helpful tool. I found duplicate content when long session is reconnected. So I try this fix.

## Summary
- **Server (`pty-manager.js`)**: Replay scrollback buffer BEFORE adding the client to the broadcast set. Previously, the client was added first, allowing live PTY data to interleave with the historical scrollback replay — causing duplicated content for long sessions.
- **Client (`terminal.js`)**: Cancel pending write timers (`_writeRaf`, `_bgFlushTimer`) and clear the write buffer before `term.reset()` on reconnect. A stale background flush timer could fire after the terminal was cleared, writing old data back onto the clean screen.
title: Fix terminal scrollback duplication on WebSocket reconnect

body:
The scroll handler was directly manipulating `xterm-viewport.scrollTop`, bypassing xterm.js's internal scroll state (ydisp). This meant xterm.js didn't know the user had scrolled up, so every new PTY output line snapped the view back to the bottom — making it impossible to scroll through text.

Fix: use term.scrollLines() (xterm.js's own API) which keeps ydisp in sync and enables xterm.js's built-in scroll lock, stopping auto-follow on output.

Also fix momentum:
- Time-based decay using actual rAF timestamps (works at 60/90/120Hz)
- Lower MIN_VELOCITY threshold (0.5→0.1 px/ms) so slow swipes get momentum
- Sub-line pixel accumulator for smooth fractional-line scrolling
- FRICTION 0.95→0.92 for a snappier feel
title: fix: mobile terminal scroll snaps back to bottom on new output

body:
On Linux/macOS, Claude encodes project paths by replacing / with - (e.g. /home/vivi/pingterra → -home-vivi-pingterra).  `decodeClaudePath` only handled Windows drive-letter paths and returned the encoded string as-is for everything else, which got stored as `workingDir` and caused PTY spawn to fail with "cwd does not exist".

The fix adds a Linux/macOS branch that strips the leading - and runs the same greedy filesystem walk from /. Also extracted the shared walk logic into a `greedyFsWalk` helper.
title: fix: decodeClaudePath not handling Linux/macOS paths

## Summary

Adds Cloudflare named tunnel support so Myrlin can be accessed over the internet via a persistent custom domain.

- New **Remote Access** settings category in Settings panel
- Inline 4-step setup guide pointing users to the CF dashboard with exact values (Type=HTTP, URL=localhost:3456)
- Token stored server-side in `~/.myrlin/config.json` (merge-safe, never returned by API)
- `cloudflared tunnel run --token` managed as a Myrlin subprocess with start/stop/auto-start
- Live status indicator (🟢 connected / 🟡 connecting / ⚫ stopped) via SSE

## New API endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/api/tunnel/named` | Status + `configured`/`autoStart` flags |
| `PUT` | `/api/tunnel/named/config` | Save token + autoStart setting |
| `POST` | `/api/tunnel/named/start` | Start `cloudflared` subprocess |
| `POST` | `/api/tunnel/named/stop` | Stop tunnel (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) |

## How to use

1. `brew install cloudflared`
2. Settings → Remote Access → follow the 4-step guide
3. Create a tunnel at [one.dash.cloudflare.com](https://one.dash.cloudflare.com) → Networks → Tunnels
4. Public hostname: subdomain of your choice, Type `HTTP`, URL `localhost:3456`
5. Paste the `eyJ…` token → Save → Start

## Test plan

- [ ] Token saves without overwriting existing config keys (e.g. password)
- [ ] Start/Stop buttons update status indicator via SSE
- [ ] Auto-start launches tunnel on server init
- [ ] `CWM_CF_TOKEN` env var overrides stored config
- [ ] `GET /api/tunnel/named` never exposes the raw token value
title: feat: Cloudflare named tunnel integration (named tunnel + UI setup guide)

Closes #8

## Summary

- `spawnSession()` catches PTY spawn errors internally and returns `null` instead of throwing
- `attachClient()`'s `try/catch` only handles thrown exceptions, so a null session fell through silently to `session.clients.add(ws)`
- This crashed with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'clients')`, caught by the store's `uncaughtException` handler and logged as `[Store] Uncaught exception, flushing state`

## Fix

Added an explicit `if (!session)` null guard in `attachClient()` immediately after the spawn try/catch block. On null, sends a `{ type: 'error' }` JSON message to the WebSocket client and closes cleanly — consistent with the existing exception handling path.

## Reproducer

Drag a discovered session whose worktree directory has been deleted or whose PTY process fails to start (`posix_spawnp failed`). Before this fix the server would crash the store; after, the client receives a clean error and the server stays stable.

## Test plan

- [ ] Start Myrlin, drag a discovered session with a valid cwd → session opens normally
- [ ] Drag a discovered session whose cwd is stale/missing → client receives error toast, server stays up, no `[Store] Uncaught exception` in logs
title: fix: guard against null session from spawnSession in attachClient

body:
Korean (and other CJK) input duplicated the last composed character when pressing space — e.g. "한글" became "한글글".

The compositionend handler was sending e.data directly via WebSocket, but xterm.js v6's CompositionHelper already emits the composed text through onData internally.  This created two send paths for the same character.  The _composing flag guarding onData could not resolve this: clearing it synchronously still allowed the duplicate through, and deferring the clear blocked legitimate text because Korean IME fires compositionstart for the next syllable before the previous syllable's deferred onData arrives.

Remove the compositionstart/compositionend listeners and the _composing guard on onData entirely, letting xterm.js's CompositionHelper be the sole owner of IME composition handling.
title: Fix CJK composition duplicate input in web terminal

## Summary
- **Scroll fix**: Hidden xterm scrollbar on mobile (conflicts with Chrome's right-edge gestures) and added `stopPropagation()` to capture-phase touch handlers so xterm.js can't fight the manual scroll
- **Input fix**: Added a dedicated mobile input field (`<input>`) that bypasses xterm.js's hidden textarea entirely — autocorrect, swipe typing, and tap-to-correct suggestions all work without text duplication
- **LAN/Tailscale access**: CORS and CSP headers are now dynamic based on the request host, so the GUI works when accessed via Tailscale or other LAN IPs (not just localhost)

## Context
On mobile Chrome, xterm.js's hidden textarea doesn't handle autocorrect properly — when the keyboard replaces text (via composition events or `insertReplacementText`), xterm processes both the original keystrokes and the replacement, causing entire phrases to duplicate. This is a fundamental mismatch between how mobile keyboards expect textareas to work and how xterm.js uses its textarea as a transient input pipe.

Rather than trying to patch xterm.js's event handling (which proved unreliable across keyboard implementations), the mobile "Type" button now toggles a real `<input>` field above the toolbar. Text is composed there with full autocorrect support, then sent to the PTY on Enter/Send.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open on mobile Chrome, tap Type, verify the input field appears and autocorrect works without duplication
- [ ] Verify scroll mode still works smoothly (no xterm scrollbar visible, momentum scrolling intact)
- [ ] Access via Tailscale/LAN IP — verify WebSocket connects and terminals work
- [ ] Desktop behavior unchanged (input field is mobile-only via media query)

## Summary

- **Upgrade deprecated xterm packages** to their maintained `@xterm/*` scoped equivalents (`@xterm/xterm@6.0.0`, `@xterm/addon-fit@0.11.0`, `@xterm/addon-web-links@0.12.0`). The old `xterm`, `xterm-addon-fit`, and `xterm-addon-web-links` packages are deprecated. Vendor files updated from the new packages.

- **Fix session cwd resolution in PTY manager** — when the PTY manager receives an encoded directory name as cwd (e.g. `-Users-jane-project`), it now resolves the real working directory from Claude's `sessions-index.json` (`originalPath` / per-entry `projectPath`) before falling back to home. Also scans the JSONL `cwd` field as a last resort.

- **Fix project path resolution in server.js** — `decodeClaudePath()` only handled Windows-style encoded paths (starting with a drive letter like `C--Users-...`). On macOS/Linux, encoded names were returned unchanged, causing incorrect paths in the discover endpoint, search, and session file listing. Added `resolveProjectPath()` which reads `originalPath` from `sessions-index.json` first (works on all platforms), falling back to `decodeClaudePath()` for legacy compatibility. Updated all 3 call sites.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `npm install` — verify no deprecation warnings
- [ ] Start the GUI (`npm run gui`) — verify terminals render correctly with xterm 6
- [ ] Open a session with an encoded project path — verify it spawns in the correct working directory instead of `~`
- [ ] Verify the discover page (`/api/discover`) shows correct `realPath` values on macOS/Linux
- [ ] Open a session with a normal cwd — verify no regression
title: Upgrade xterm to v6 + fix session cwd resolution
